newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-DISAPPOINTED BAGGIO SAYS HE LEAVING AC MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DISAPPOINTED BAGGIO SAYS HE LEAVING AC MILAN.

text.p: Italian midfielder Roberto Baggio said on Wednesday he was disappointed to be leaving AC Milan.

Interviewed by Italy's RAI television at Venice airport on his return from a holiday in Argentina, the ponytailed World Cup star confirmed his generally-expected departure but did not say what he planned to do next season.
Asked when he had realised that his days at Milan were over, Baggio replied: "When (coach Fabio) Capello rang me on the telephone. He confirmed a bit what was in the air.
"I was expecting it a bit...of course I'm disappointed a bit, breaking with the fans.
"In our business you have to come to terms with so many situations, even unthinkable ones perhaps."

Italian newspapers reported earlier this week that Capello, returning after a season at Real Madrid, had told Baggio and Yugoslav forward Dejan Savicevic that there would be no place for them at the club next season.
Baggio, 30, joined Milan in 1995, weeks after helping Juventus to the league title at the end of his fifth season with the Turin club.

He repeated the feat under Capello at Milan the following season but was left on the substitutes bench for much of Milan's disappointing last campaign, firstly by Uruguayan coach Oscar Tabarez and then by Arrigo Sacchi.
His relationship with former Italy boss Sacchi was strained and it seemed only a matter of time before he left the San Siro.
Baggio said on Wednesday no Milan official had contacted him to break the news, other than Capello.
"When they need you, they call you even at home. When you are no longer any use, the telephone ceases to exist," he said.
Asked which club was closest to him now, Baggio replied with a laugh: "The nearest is Vicenza, because I live there."
Baggio has been linked in recent weeks to several clubs, including Napoli and Spain's Barcelona.
He has reportedly ruled out a move to Japan or the United States.
Vicenza, the club where he started his soccer career and where he played for three seasons, were last week sold at auction to British investment company Stellican.
Baggio, who missed a penalty with the last kick of the 1994 World Cup final to give the title to Brazil, has said he dearly wants to play in the finals in France next year.
He therefore needs regular first team football, which he would almost certainly get at either Napoli or Vicenza.

However, both clubs were in a financial straight-jacket last season and it remains to be seen whether either can, or are willing to, pay his wages as well as the sizeable transfer fee Milan are bound to demand.

Italy's Gianfranco Zola, who played at Napoli with Diego Maradona, has repeatedly encouraged Baggio to consider moving to the southern club, saying that it is the sort of city whose fans appreciate an exceptional talent such as Baggio's.
